commands.short: List open dead letters
commands.long:
List the open dead letters: messages a consumer gave up on, outbox rows a
relay could not publish, and stream entries trimmed before a consumer group
finished them.

Use when the user asks what failed to process, what is in the dead-letter
queue, or whether any messages were lost.

Arguments:
  [source]  Optional. consumer, outbox, quarantine, or all. Omit (or give
            all) to list every source; an empty value is a usage error.
  [stream]  Optional. Only dead letters of this stream, e.g. task.status.updated:v2.
            Omit to list every stream; an empty value is a usage error. To
            filter by stream alone, give all as the source.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"total_open":number,"dead_letters":[{"id":string,"source":string,
   "failure_kind":string,"stream":string,"group":string,
   "original_message_id":string,"producer":string,"error":string,
   "delivery_count":number,"original_at":string,"recorded_at":string,
   "expires_at":string,"status":string,"redrivable":boolean,
   "not_redrivable_reason":string,"redrive":null}]}
  At most 50 dead letters, newest first. total_open counts every open one.
  redrivable is false, and not_redrivable_reason says why, for a dead letter
  that can never be redriven: its stream was retired, the streams contract
  does not name its stream or consumer group, or its fields are not a
  message.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  more than two arguments, a blank argument, or an unknown source
  unavailable(exit 5)  dead-letter-controller is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Republish dead letters to their original stream
commands.long:
Republish dead letters to the stream they came from, so the consumer group
that failed them processes them again (an outbox dead letter, never published,
goes to every group of its stream).

Use when the user asks to retry, replay or redrive failed messages, after the
cause was fixed.

Arguments:
  <ids>     One dead letter id, or several separated by commas, as listed by
            "dlq list". Either all are redriven or none is.
  <reason>  Why they are redriven; recorded with the redrive. Required and
            must be non-empty.

The redriving identity is not an argument: it is taken from the
CONTINUO_ACTOR environment variable when set, otherwise dead-letter-controller
records its own system identity. A dead letter already redriven is returned
unchanged.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"dead_letters":[{...same object as dlq list, status "redriven" and redrive set...}]}

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, no ids, a blank reason, or an id
                       that is not a dead letter id
  not_found  (exit 3)  an id matches no dead letter (nothing was redriven)
  conflict   (exit 4)  a dead letter is older than the 30-day replay horizon, or can
                       never be redriven (dlq list shows why; nothing was redriven)
  unavailable(exit 5)  dead-letter-controller is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; new work is refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Run and test a model node with dbt build
commands.long:
Run and test a model node with dbt build.

Use when the user asks to build a specific dbt model now, as opposed to only
testing it. dbt build both materializes (runs) the model and runs its tests
in one invocation. There is no "no_tests" skip for a single-node build: a
model with no tests defined is still built. By default the run uses the
model's current (latest) image and manifest version. Pass a past run id to
build the model exactly as that run saw it.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.
  [source-run-id]  Optional. The id of a past run of this node, as listed by
                   "node history". When given, the new run reuses the image
                   and manifest version that run used ("snapshot_of_run"
                   metadata) instead of the latest topology. The source run
                   must have finished (succeeded, failed or cancelled) and
                   must have included this node. Omit the argument for
                   latest mode; an empty value is a usage error.

The initiating identity is not an argument: it is taken from the CONTINUO_ACTOR
environment variable when set, otherwise the state service records its own
system identity.

This command reports acceptance, not completion. On success the new run is
planned and durably recorded with its first dispatches; a node the live
release does not hold is refused (not_found) and no run is created.
A task whose node another run is writing waits for that run to finish
writing it before it is dispatched: "node history" and "schedule status" show
the task pending, with wait_reason "node_lease" and the run it waits on
(waiting_on_run_id).
Check the outcome of an accepted run with "node history".

Each invocation sends one request id (the CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID environment
variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:
any other value is refused (usage, exit 2). The state service answers a repeat
of the same id and the same arguments with the run the first call started or
cancelled and writes nothing, so a lost response is safe to retry. The same id
with other arguments is refused (conflict, exit 4, not retryable): no retry of
it can succeed, so send other arguments under a new id. A call refused because
the state service is unavailable, or because concurrent calls of the same id
kept rolling back, is sent again with the same id up to twice before it is
reported (unavailable or conflict, retryable).

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string}

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, a malformed source run id, or the server rejects the identity triple
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node is not in the release the run would use, or the source run does not exist
  conflict   (exit 4)  the source run has not finished yet, the node's schedule has an active run, or the request id was used before with other arguments
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; new work is refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: List a shared-code unit's (or a node's units') version chain
commands.long:
List a shared-code unit's version chain, newest first.

Use when the user wants the history of a dbt macro (or other shared-code
unit): every recorded checksum, its source, and the release that promoted it.

This command takes exactly one of two mutually exclusive selectors:

  <unit-id>                              query one unit's chain directly.
  --service <s> --schema <s> --table <t> resolve the named node's CURRENT
                                          units first, then return each of
                                          their chains concatenated in
                                          resolution order. All three flags
                                          are required together; the node is
                                          addressed by its unique_id,
                                          "<schema>.<table>" ( --service is
                                          accepted for consistency with the
                                          other node subcommands but does not
                                          appear in the unique_id).

Supplying both the positional <unit-id> and any of --service/--schema/--table,
or supplying neither, is a usage error — there is no default selector.

Flags:
  --service  Owning service name of the node whose units to list. Must be
             combined with --schema and --table; mutually exclusive with
             <unit-id>.
  --schema   Schema name of the node whose units to list. Must be combined
             with --service and --table; mutually exclusive with <unit-id>.
  --table    Table (model) name of the node whose units to list. Must be
             combined with --service and --schema; mutually exclusive with
             <unit-id>.
  --limit    Maximum number of versions returned per unit, newest first.
             Default 20; the server also applies this default when sent 0,
             and clamps any value above 200 down to 200.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"versions":[{"unit_id":string,"checksum":string,"source":string,
   "repo":string,"commit_sha":string,"release_id":string,
   "promoted_at":string,"is_current":bool}]}
  repo, commit_sha, release_id, promoted_at, and is_current are omitted when
  the version carries no value for them.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of positional arguments, or the selector is not exactly one of <unit-id> / --service+--schema+--table
  not_found  (exit 3)  the unit_id, or the node's unique_id, is not recorded
  unavailable(exit 5)  the orchestrator service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Render the diff between two recorded versions of one model node
commands.long:
Render the diff between two recorded versions of one model node.

Use when the user wants to see exactly what changed between two code versions
of a dbt model: the raw source diff, the config diff, and which of source,
shared code, and config actually changed.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.

The node is addressed by its unique_id, "<schema>.<table>"; <service> is
accepted for consistency with the other node subcommands but does not appear
in the unique_id.

Flags:
  --from  Required. The version_seq to diff from. version_seq is a stable
          per-node handle used to address a version — it is NOT a
          chronological ordering, and --from need not be the older version.
  --to    Required. The version_seq to diff to. Same handle semantics as
          --from.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"unique_id":string,
   "from":{...version object, same shape as "node versions"...},
   "to":{...version object, same shape as "node versions"...},
   "raw_code_diff":string,"config_diff":string,"source_changed":bool,
   "shared_code_changed":bool,"config_changed":bool,"truncated":bool}
  raw_code_diff and config_diff are omitted when that part is unchanged.
  truncated is set when either diff was cut to the server's per-diff 8 KiB cap.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, missing --from/--to, or --from equals --to
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node's unique_id, or one of the two seqs, is not recorded
  unavailable(exit 5)  the orchestrator service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Rebuild one dbt model or seed from scratch (dbt --full-refresh)
commands.long:
Rebuild one dbt model or seed from scratch (dbt --full-refresh).

Use when the user asks to fully refresh, rebuild from scratch, or re-create a
specific dbt model or seed — for example an incremental model whose logic or
columns changed, whose normal runs only insert new rows. The node's production
table is dropped and rebuilt. Only this node runs; continuo does not trigger its
upstream or downstream nodes. On Postgres, views that select from the node are
dropped with it until their own models run again. Only dbt models and dbt seeds
can be fully refreshed; snapshots, dbt tests and python nodes are rejected.
By default the run uses the node's current (latest) image and manifest version.
Pass a past run id to rebuild the node exactly as that run saw it.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model or seed) name.
  [source-run-id]  Optional. The id of a past run of this node, as listed by
                   "node history". When given, the new run reuses the image
                   and manifest version that run used ("snapshot_of_run"
                   metadata) instead of the latest topology. The source run
                   must have finished (succeeded, failed or cancelled) and
                   must have included this node. Omit the argument for
                   latest mode; an empty value is a usage error.

The initiating identity is not an argument: it is taken from the CONTINUO_ACTOR
environment variable when set, otherwise the state service records its own
system identity.

This command reports acceptance, not completion. On success the new run is
planned and durably recorded with its first dispatches. A node the live
release does not hold is refused (not_found), and a node that is not a dbt
model or seed is refused (usage); neither creates a run. If the node's service
governing command block defines no full_refresh (model) or seed_full_refresh
(seed) command, the run is accepted and fails when it executes.
A task whose node another run is writing waits for that run to finish
writing it before it is dispatched: "node history" and "schedule status" show
the task pending, with wait_reason "node_lease" and the run it waits on
(waiting_on_run_id).
Check the outcome of an accepted run with "node history".

Each invocation sends one request id (the CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID environment
variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:
any other value is refused (usage, exit 2). The state service answers a repeat
of the same id and the same arguments with the run the first call started or
cancelled and writes nothing, so a lost response is safe to retry. The same id
with other arguments is refused (conflict, exit 4, not retryable): no retry of
it can succeed, so send other arguments under a new id. A call refused because
the state service is unavailable, or because concurrent calls of the same id
kept rolling back, is sent again with the same id up to twice before it is
reported (unavailable or conflict, retryable).

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string}

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, a malformed source run id, or the server rejects the identity triple
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node is not in the release the run would use, or the source run does not exist
  conflict   (exit 4)  the source run has not finished yet, the node's schedule has an active run, or the request id was used before with other arguments
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; new work is refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: List the recent run history of one model node
commands.long:
List the recent run history of one model node.

Use when the user wants to see the last runs of a specific dbt model, including
whether each run succeeded, which attempt the task reached, why its latest
attempt failed (failure class, reason and error message), which image it ran,
its log and result locations, and the content hash of the code it executed.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.

Flags:
  --operation  Filter history to one operation kind: run | test | build.
               Default "run" (dbt run/materialize rows). "test" returns dbt
               test rows; "build" returns dbt build rows. An unrecognized
               value is a usage error.

Output (stdout, JSON): up to 50 runs, newest first.
  {"runs":[{"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string,"kind":string,
   "run_status":string,"task_id":string,"task_status":string,
   "attempt":number,"image_tag":string,
   "created_at":string,"started_at":string,"completed_at":string,
   "error_message":string,"failure_class":string,"failure_reason":string,
   "log_s3_key":string,"run_results_uri":string,"operation":string,
   "content_hash":string,
   "wait_reason":string,"waiting_on_run_id":string,"waiting_since":string}]}
  attempt is the zero-based number of the task's current attempt (0 on the
  first try). run_status is the run's status: pending|running|cancelling|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  task_status is one of: pending|dispatched|queued|running|stopping|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  failure_class and failure_reason say why the latest attempt
  failed. run_status, started_at, completed_at, error_message,
  failure_class, failure_reason, log_s3_key, run_results_uri, and content_hash
  are omitted when empty. run_results_uri points at the structured result
  block the run's container printed — python-family nodes (python-node,
  python-csv, python-api) always emit one, dbt nodes never do. An unknown node returns {"runs":[]}, not an error.

content_hash is the node's content hash in the release the run ran on, as
the state service records it; it is omitted for runs that name no release.

wait_reason is node_lease while the task waits for another run to release its node:
another run's task is writing this node, and this run's pending task starts
once that write ends. waiting_on_run_id is the run writing the node (empty
for a moment when the node has just been freed and the task is about to be
granted it); waiting_since is when the wait began (RFC3339). The three are
omitted when the task waits for nothing besides its upstreams.

In --human mode, content_hash is rendered too: each line ends with an
EXECUTED_HASH column (the first 12 characters of content_hash, or "-" when
it is unavailable).

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, or --operation is not run|test|build
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: List the node catalog with per-node run statistics
commands.long:
List the node catalog with per-node run statistics, one page at a time.

Use when the user names a model but not its service or schema, wants to know
which nodes exist in a service, or asks how reliable or slow a model has been.
Each row carries the (service, schema, table) triple every other node
subcommand takes as arguments, so this is the command that resolves a bare
table name into an addressable node.

Statistics cover each node's most recent 50 tasks of the selected operation.

Arguments: none. Every filter is a flag.

Flags:
  --search     Table name to look up. Case-insensitive EXACT match on the
               table name, not a substring: "orders" matches "orders" and
               "Orders", never "orders_daily". Default "" (no filter).
  --service    Exact service name. Default "" (all services).
  --operation  Which operation's tasks feed the statistics: run | test |
               build. Default "run". An unrecognized value is a usage error.
  --limit      Page size, 1..200. Default 50. A value outside that range is
               a usage error.
  --offset     Number of matching rows to skip, >= 0. Default 0.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"total_count":number,
   "nodes":[{"service_name":string,"schema_name":string,"table_name":string,
   "task_count":number,"success_rate_pct":number,"avg_duration_sec":number,
   "p95_duration_sec":number,"flaky_rate_pct":number,"last_status":string,
   "last_run_at":string,"operation":string,"timeout_seconds":number,
   "timeout_declared":bool}]}
  task_count is the number of the node's tasks in the statistics window (at
  most 50). total_count is the number of nodes matching the filters regardless of
  paging; when it exceeds offset + len(nodes), request the next page with a
  larger --offset. success_rate_pct is omitted when the node has no terminal
  task in the window; avg_duration_sec and p95_duration_sec are omitted when
  no task in the window was timed; last_run_at is omitted when the node has
  never run. last_status is one of succeeded, failed, running, stopping, queued,
  dispatched, cancelled, skipped, pending. timeout_seconds is the task
  timeout the node's tasks get, always present: its declared timeout in the
  live release when timeout_declared is true, else the install default. No
  match returns {"total_count":0,"nodes":[]}, not an error.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  a positional argument was given, --operation is not
                       run|test|build, --limit is outside 1..200, or --offset
                       is negative
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

flags.name: limit
flags.usage: Page size, 1..200 (default 50)

flags.name: offset
flags.usage: Number of matching rows to skip (default 0)

flags.name: operation

commands.short: Run a model node's dbt tests
commands.long:
Run a model node's dbt tests.

Use when the user asks to test, validate, or check a specific dbt model now,
as opposed to running (building) it. The run dispatches dbt test rather than
dbt run/build for that single node. By default it uses the model's current
(latest) image and manifest version. Pass a past run id to test the model
exactly as that run saw it.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.
  [source-run-id]  Optional. The id of a past run of this node, as listed by
                   "node history". When given, the new run reuses the image
                   and manifest version that run used ("snapshot_of_run"
                   metadata) instead of the latest topology. The source run
                   must have finished (succeeded, failed or cancelled) and
                   must have included this node. Omit the argument for
                   latest mode; an empty value is a usage error.

The initiating identity is not an argument: it is taken from the CONTINUO_ACTOR
environment variable when set, otherwise the state service records its own
system identity.

This command reports acceptance, not completion. On success the new run is
planned and durably recorded with its first dispatches. A node the live
release does not hold is refused (not_found). A model with no data tests
(in the live release, or in the source run's release when one is given) is
refused (conflict). Neither refusal creates a run. Check the outcome of an
accepted run with "node history".

Each invocation sends one request id (the CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID environment
variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:
any other value is refused (usage, exit 2). The state service answers a repeat
of the same id and the same arguments with the run the first call started or
cancelled and writes nothing, so a lost response is safe to retry. The same id
with other arguments is refused (conflict, exit 4, not retryable): no retry of
it can succeed, so send other arguments under a new id. A call refused because
the state service is unavailable, or because concurrent calls of the same id
kept rolling back, is sent again with the same id up to twice before it is
reported (unavailable or conflict, retryable).

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string}

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, a malformed source run id, or the server rejects the identity triple
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node is not in the release the run would use, or the source run does not exist
  conflict   (exit 4)  the source run has not finished yet, the node's schedule has an active run, or the request id was used before with other arguments
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; new work is refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: List a model node's ancestors' most recent code changes
commands.long:
List a model node's ancestors' most recent code changes, most-recently-changed first.

Use when the user wants to know what changed upstream of a failing or
suspicious dbt model: which ancestors changed, how recently, and what their
diff looks like.

"Most recently changed" is each ancestor's EFFECTIVE last change, not a
version's own creation time: a version node is immutable, so a revert that
re-points an ancestor's running code at an already-recorded version still
counts as a change at the moment of the revert, and the reported diff is that
revert's actual before/after rather than the two versions' original creation
order.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.

The node is addressed by its unique_id, "<schema>.<table>"; <service> is
accepted for consistency with the other node subcommands but does not appear
in the unique_id.

Contract caps (enforced server-side, not adjustable): results are capped at
the 5 most-recently-changed ancestors, and each diff is independently capped
at 8 KiB with its own truncated flag set on the diffs that were cut — size
prompts against both caps, not just the top-level result count.

Flags:
  --depth  How many hops upstream to walk. <= 0 (the default) applies the
           server's default of 3 hops. The server rejects any value above 10
           as invalid — this is a hard cap, not a client-side clamp.
  --since  RFC3339 timestamp; ancestors whose effective last change (see
           above — a revert counts) predates it are excluded. Empty (the
           default) applies no time filter.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"changes":[{"unique_id":string,"depth":number,
   "diff":{...diff object, same shape as "node diff"...}}]}

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, --depth above 10, or --since is not RFC3339
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node's unique_id is not recorded
  unavailable(exit 5)  the orchestrator service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

flags.name: depth
flags.usage: Hops upstream to walk; <= 0 applies the server default of 3, values above 10 are rejected

flags.name: since
flags.usage: RFC3339 timestamp; excludes ancestors whose newest version predates it (default: no filter)

commands.short: List a model node's recorded code-version history
commands.long:
List a model node's recorded code-version history, newest first.

Use when the user wants to see what code a dbt model has run over time: every
recorded version's hashes, the release that promoted it, and (with
--include-code) the code itself.

Newest first means ordered by when each version's code was FIRST promoted,
not by when it last ran: a version node is immutable, so a revert to earlier
code re-points at the version that already exists rather than moving it in
this list. is_current marks the version that actually runs now — after a
revert, that can be a version further down this list, not the first row.

Arguments:
  <service>  The owning service name.
  <schema>   The schema name.
  <table>    The table (model) name.

The node is addressed by its unique_id, "<schema>.<table>"; <service> is
accepted for consistency with the other node subcommands but does not appear
in the unique_id, matching how the orchestrator tracks version history.

Flags:
  --limit         Maximum number of versions returned, newest first. Default
                   20; the server also applies this default when sent 0, and
                   clamps any value above 200 down to 200.
  --include-code  Include raw_code/compiled_code in the response. Default
                   false: both fields come back empty and every other field
                   (hashes, config_json, provenance) is unaffected. A single
                   version's compiled_code can run to 256 KiB, so leave this
                   off unless the code itself is needed.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"versions":[{"unique_id":string,"version_seq":number,"content_hash":string,
   "source_hash":string,"shared_code_hash":string,"config_hash":string,
   "runtime":string,"raw_code":string,"compiled_code":string,
   "compiled_truncated":bool,"config_json":string,"repo":string,
   "commit_sha":string,"release_id":string,"promoted_at":string,
   "healed":bool,"backfilled":bool,"is_current":bool}]}
  raw_code and compiled_code are empty unless --include-code is set.
  compiled_code, compiled_truncated, repo, commit_sha, release_id,
  promoted_at, healed, backfilled, and is_current are omitted when the
  version carries no value for them (e.g. a version with no release
  provenance, or one that is not the node's current version).

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments
  not_found  (exit 3)  the node's unique_id is not recorded
  unavailable(exit 5)  the orchestrator service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Look up how a classified failure was rejected and fixed before
commands.long:
Look up how a classified failure was rejected and fixed before.

Use when an LLM needs to answer "how was this exact error solved before?" for
a validation rejection: has this same failure signature — or the same
(category, reason) pair — been seen and resolved on a prior release, and if
so, what changed to fix it.

Arguments:
  signature  Optional positional form of --signature. At most one positional
             argument is accepted.

Selectors (precedence: --signature, then the positional signature, then
--category/--reason):
  --signature  The exact classifier signature to match. Wins over a
               positional signature when both are given.
  --category   Together with --reason, matches every rejection sharing that
               (category, reason) pair. Both must be set to use this form.
  --reason     See --category.

Flags:
  --limit         Caps the number of precedents returned, resolved-first then
                  newest. 0 (the default) applies the server default of 5;
                  the server clamps the maximum to 20 — this command does not
                  re-implement that clamp client-side.
  --include-code  Also return the failing candidate's raw code and the
                  resolving version's raw code. The error excerpt and the
                  resolution diff are ALWAYS included regardless of this
                  flag; the diff is capped server-side at 8 KiB with a
                  truncated flag set on any diff that was cut.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"precedents":[{"release_id":string,"node_id":string,"stage":string,
   "category":string,"reason":string,"error_excerpt":string,
   "rejected_at":string,"failing_code":string,"resolved":bool,
   "resolving_version":{"version_seq":number,"content_hash":string,
   "release_id":string,"repo":string,"commit_sha":string,
   "promoted_at":string,"raw_code":string},"resolution_diff":string,
   "resolution_diff_truncated":bool,
   "proposals":[{"proposal_id":string,"pr_url":string,"pr_number":number,
   "pr_state":string}]}]}
  failing_code and resolving_version.raw_code are only populated when
  --include-code is set. resolving_version is omitted when resolved is false.
  proposals[].pr_state records the proposal's state when the PR was opened
  (e.g. "open") — it is NOT updated when the PR is later merged or closed, so
  it must not be read as the PR's current state.

An unknown signature — or an unseen (category, reason) pair — is NOT an
error: it returns an empty precedents list with exit 0, because "no
precedent" is a valid answer to the question this command asks.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  more than one positional argument was given, or
                        neither a signature (--signature or positional) nor a
                        complete --category and --reason pair was given
  unavailable(exit 5)  the orchestrator service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.long:
List the attempts of a run's tasks, or of one task.

Use when the user asks why a task failed, how often it was retried, how long an
attempt took, or where its logs and results are. "run show" gives each task's
latest failure; this lists every attempt with its timings and error.

Arguments:
  <run-id>   The UUID of the run.
  [task-id]  Optional. The UUID of one task of the run (the task_id of "run graph");
             only that task's attempts are listed. A blank value is refused.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"attempts":[{"task_id":string,"attempt":number,"job_name":string,"status":string,
                "failure_class":string,"failure_reason":string,"exit_code":number,
                "dispatched_at":string,"queued_at":string,"started_at":string,
                "finished_at":string,"execution_seconds":number,"error_message":string,
                "log_s3_key":string,"run_results_uri":string}],
   "total_count":number}
  Attempts are ordered by task id, then attempt number (0-based). status is one of
  dispatched|queued|running|succeeded|failed|stopped. failure_class and failure_reason
  are set only for a failed attempt; a timestamp, error_message, log_s3_key and
  run_results_uri are omitted until recorded. Timestamps are RFC3339 in UTC.
  exit_code 0 is a clean exit only for a succeeded attempt; it is also what an
  unknown exit code reads as.
  The output is ONE page of at most 200 attempts, in that order. total_count counts every
  attempt the filter matches: when it exceeds the length of "attempts", the list is
  truncated, so name a task-id to read one task's attempts.
  An unknown run, or a task the run does not have, lists nothing and exits 0.

  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, a blank task id, or an id that is not a UUID
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Cancel one run by id; it ends cancelled once its Jobs have stopped
commands.long:
Cancel one run by id.

Use when the user asks to stop, cancel or kill a particular run, for example a
run found with "run show" or "schedule runs". To cancel whatever run a schedule
has active now, use "schedule cancel".

A successful cancel means the run is now cancelling, not that it has stopped:
the state service stops handing out work, and the run ends cancelled once
execution-controller has stopped every Job of it. Until then the run's status is
cancelling and its tasks that were running show as stopping; read "run show
<run-id>" to see when the run has ended. A run with nothing in flight ends
cancelled at once.
A second cancel of a cancelling run succeeds and changes nothing: it returns the same
run and keeps the first cancel's time, author and reason. The same holds for a
run that is already cancelled.

Arguments:
  <run-id>  The UUID of the run to cancel.
  <reason>  Why the run is being cancelled; recorded for audit. Required and
            must be non-empty.

The cancelling identity is not an argument: it is taken from the CONTINUO_ACTOR
environment variable when set, otherwise the state service records its own
system identity. This command sends no request id.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run":{"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string,"kind":string,"operation":string,
          "status":string,"failure_reason":string,"release_id":string,
          "promotion_seq":number,"initiated_by":string,"created_at":string,
          "started_at":string,"completed_at":string,"last_progress_at":string,
          "cancelled_at":string,"cancelled_by":string,"cancellation_reason":string}}
  The run is as the cancel left it: status cancelling while an attempt is still
  being stopped, cancelled when nothing was in flight. Timestamps are RFC3339 in
  UTC; failure_reason, release_id, initiated_by, the timestamps other than
  created_at and the cancel fields are omitted when empty.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, a blank run id or reason, or the run id is not a UUID
  not_found  (exit 3)  no run with that id
  conflict   (exit 4)  the run already ended succeeded, failed or skipped, so there is nothing to cancel
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Restart a failed or cancelled run from its failure on the live release
commands.long:
Restart a failed or cancelled run from its failure on the live release.

Use when the user asks to restart a failed or cancelled run from its failure on
the newest code. Always run "run rebase-preview" first, show the user its counts
(how many nodes run, how many are new, changed upstream or inherited), ask for
approval, and only then run this command with the release_id the preview printed.
The release id makes the approval binding: if the live release moved since the
preview, the rebase is refused and nothing is started.

The new run keeps the source's schedule name and runs on the live release. It
re-executes the source's tasks that did not succeed, the live schedule's nodes
the source never ran, everything below them and, with with-changed-upstream,
every changed node upstream of those. Every other success is inherited.

Arguments:
  <run-id>                The UUID of the failed or cancelled run to rebase from.
  <release-id>            The release_id "run rebase-preview" printed, which must still
                          be the live release. Required and must be non-empty.
  [with-changed-upstream] Optional: "true" or "false" (default false); pass the value
                          that was previewed. Any other value is refused.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string}
  run_id is the id of the new run; schedule_name is the source run's schedule.

Each invocation sends one request id (the CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID environment
variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:
any other value is refused (usage, exit 2). The state service answers a repeat

commands.short: Show one run and the status and failure of each of its tasks
commands.long:
Show one run and the status and failure of each of its tasks.

Use when the user asks how a run is going, why it failed, or which of its nodes
ran, failed, waited or were skipped. To find a run id, use "schedule status"
(the latest run of a schedule) or "schedule runs" (its completed runs).

Arguments:
  <run-id>  The UUID of the run.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run":{"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string,"kind":string,"operation":string,
          "status":string,"failure_reason":string,"release_id":string,
          "promotion_seq":number,"initiated_by":string,"created_at":string,
          "started_at":string,"completed_at":string,"last_progress_at":string,
          "cancelled_at":string,"cancelled_by":string,"cancellation_reason":string},
   "tasks":[{"node":string,"status":string,"attempt":number,
             "failure_class":string,"failure_reason":string,
             "wait_reason":string,"waiting_on_run_id":string}]}
  Timestamps are RFC3339 in UTC. failure_reason, release_id, initiated_by, the
  timestamps other than created_at and the cancel fields are omitted when empty.
  kind is one of cron|trigger|rerun|rebase|single_node_run|promote_seed;
  operation is one of run|test|build|full_refresh.
  The run status is one of pending|running|cancelling|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  cancelling: a cancel was accepted and the run waits for its Jobs to stop.
  The run's failure_reason (stalled|empty_selection|invalid_node_type) is set only
  when the run failed without a failed task.
  node is "<service>.<schema>.<table>". attempt is the 0-based number of the task's current attempt.
  status is one of: pending|dispatched|queued|running|stopping|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  dispatched: an attempt was sent and not yet accepted; queued: the attempt
  was accepted and waits for a slot to run in; stopping: a stop was requested
  and the task waits for its attempt to stop.
  failure_class and failure_reason are those of the task's latest attempt and are
  empty strings when that attempt did not fail or the task has no attempt yet.
  wait_reason is node_lease while the task waits for another run to release its node,
  and waiting_on_run_id is the run writing that node (empty for a moment when the
  node has just been freed); both are empty strings when the task waits for nothing
  besides its upstreams.

  not_found  (exit 3)  no run with that id
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, or the run id is not a UUID
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable

Use when the user asks to stop, cancel, or kill a schedule that is running now.

the state service stops handing out work, and the run ends cancelled once
execution-controller has stopped every Job of it. Until then the run's status
is cancelling and its tasks that were running show as stopping; read
"schedule status <schedule-name>" to see when the run has ended.

run and keeps the first cancel's time, author and reason.

                   and must be non-empty.

environment variable when set, otherwise the state service records its own
system identity.

  time this command received the answer, not the time of the first cancel.

variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:

cancelled and writes nothing, so a lost response is safe to retry. The same id
with other arguments is refused (conflict, exit 4, not retryable): no retry of

(pending, running or cancelling) is not listed: "schedule status" shows it.

Arguments:
  <schedule-name>  The schedule whose runs to list (exact match).

            "created_at":string,"completed_at":string,"failure_reason":string}],
   "total_count":number}
  status is one of succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped. created_at and completed_at are
  RFC3339 in UTC. failure_reason (stalled|empty_selection|invalid_node_type) is set only
  when the run failed without a failed task and is omitted otherwise.
  The output is ONE page: the newest runs, at most the server's default page size.
  total_count counts every completed run of the schedule: when it exceeds the length
  of "runs", older runs exist that this command does not list.
  A schedule with no completed run, or one that does not exist, returns "runs":[]
  and "total_count":0 with exit 0.

  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable

commands.short: Set when a schedule runs on its own: a cron in a timezone
commands.long:
Set when a schedule runs on its own: a cron in a timezone.

Use when the user asks to schedule a schedule, to change the time it runs
automatically, to add a cron to a schedule that has none (one that runs only
when triggered), or to change a cron's timezone or description. The cron decides
only WHEN the schedule runs; which models it runs comes from their dbt tag, so
the name must be a schedule that "schedule list" shows.

Arguments:
  <name>         The schedule name, exactly as "schedule list" shows it. Names
                 are case-sensitive: "Daily" is not "daily".
  <cron>         Five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) or a
                 descriptor such as @daily. Pass the five fields as ONE argument
                 (in a shell, quote it): "0 1 * * *". A CRON_TZ= or TZ= prefix
                 is refused: the timezone is the next argument.
  <timezone>     The IANA zone the cron is read in, such as Europe/Paris or UTC.
  [description]  Optional. What the schedule is for. Omit it to keep the current
                 description; an empty value is a usage error.

set-cron sets the cron and the timezone and re-sends the rest of the schedule as
listed: its current paused flag and its description (a [description] given
replaces it). A paused schedule stays paused; "schedule resume" starts it. The
next fire counts from now.
Only a schedule's first cron needs a model of the live release with its tag; a
schedule that has a cron can be changed whatever the live release holds.

For a schedule that has a cron, set-cron sends the version it read, so a
concurrent pause is not overwritten; a description you pass replaces the stored
one. When another edit saved the schedule since, set-cron reads it again, saves
once more with the pause that edit left (and its description, unless you passed
one), and exits 4 if the schedule changed again. A first cron is saved with no
version: it overwrites an edit saved between the read and the save, the last
write winning. The cron itself is last-write-wins: a cron another editor saved a
moment ago is replaced.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"schedule_name":string,"cron":string,"cron_words":string,"timezone":string,
   "description":string,"paused":bool,"version":number,"next_fire_times":[string]}
  next_fire_times are the next three fires (RFC3339, UTC), empty while the
  schedule is paused. cron_words is the cron in English and description is the
  saved description; each is omitted when empty.

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments (a cron whose fields were not passed as one argument arrives as several), a blank argument, a name longer than 50 characters, or a cron or timezone the parser refuses; the message says why (for a cron or timezone, it is the parser's)
  not_found  (exit 3)  the schedule has no cron yet and no model of the live release has its tag; a listed name that differs only by case is offered as "did you mean"
  conflict   (exit 4)  another edit saved the schedule twice while this ran ("changed by <who> while this ran; run it again"); nothing was changed by this command, so run it again
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; edits are refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Show a schedule's latest run and the status of each of its tasks
commands.long:
Show a schedule's latest run and the status of each of its tasks.

Use when the user asks where a schedule is, how far its latest run has got, which
of its nodes are running, failed, or succeeded right now, or why the run failed.
It prints what "run show" prints for the schedule's latest run, so use "run show"
with an earlier run id (from "schedule runs") to inspect an older run.

Arguments:
  <schedule-name>  The schedule to inspect (exact match).

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run":{"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string,"kind":string,"operation":string,
          "status":string,"failure_reason":string,"release_id":string,
          "promotion_seq":number,"initiated_by":string,"created_at":string,
          "started_at":string,"completed_at":string,"last_progress_at":string,
          "cancelled_at":string,"cancelled_by":string,"cancellation_reason":string},
   "tasks":[{"node":string,"status":string,"attempt":number,
             "failure_class":string,"failure_reason":string,
             "wait_reason":string,"waiting_on_run_id":string}]}
  Timestamps are RFC3339 in UTC. failure_reason, release_id, initiated_by, the
  timestamps other than created_at and the cancel fields are omitted when empty.
  kind is one of cron|trigger|rerun|rebase|single_node_run|promote_seed;
  operation is one of run|test|build|full_refresh.
  The run status is one of pending|running|cancelling|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  pending, running and cancelling mean the run still holds the schedule;
  cancelling: a cancel was accepted and the run waits for its Jobs to stop.
  The run's failure_reason (stalled|empty_selection|invalid_node_type) is set only
  when the run failed without a failed task.
  node is "<service>.<schema>.<table>". attempt is the 0-based number of the task's current attempt.
  status is one of: pending|dispatched|queued|running|stopping|succeeded|failed|cancelled|skipped.
  dispatched: an attempt was sent and not yet accepted; queued: the attempt
  was accepted and waits for a slot to run in; stopping: a stop was requested
  and the task waits for its attempt to stop.
  failure_class and failure_reason are those of the task's latest attempt and are
  empty strings when that attempt did not fail or the task has no attempt yet.
  wait_reason is node_lease while the task waits for another run to release its node:
  another run's task is writing the same node, and this pending task starts once
  that write ends. waiting_on_run_id is the run writing the node (empty for a
  moment when the node has just been freed and the task is about to be granted it);
  both are empty strings when the task waits for nothing besides its upstreams.
  A schedule that has never run returns {"run":null,"tasks":[]}.

Errors:
  not_found  (exit 3)  no schedule with that name
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error

commands.short: Run dbt tests for every model in the named schedule
commands.long:
Run dbt tests for every model in the named schedule, using the schedule's
current (latest) topology and manifest version.

Use when the user asks to test, validate, or check an entire schedule (its
whole DAG of models) now, as opposed to running (building) it. Every node in
the schedule that has dbt tests defined runs dbt test; nodes with no tests
defined are skipped rather than failed.

Arguments:
  <schedule-name>  The schedule to test.

Output (stdout, JSON):
  {"run_id":string,"schedule_name":string,"triggered_at":string}

Each invocation sends one request id (the CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID environment
variable when set, otherwise a fresh UUID). CONTINUO_REQUEST_ID must be a UUID:
any other value is refused (usage, exit 2). The state service answers a repeat
of the same id and the same arguments with the run the first call started or
cancelled and writes nothing, so a lost response is safe to retry. The same id
with other arguments is refused (conflict, exit 4, not retryable): no retry of
it can succeed, so send other arguments under a new id. A call refused because
the state service is unavailable, or because concurrent calls of the same id
kept rolling back, is sent again with the same id up to twice before it is
reported (unavailable or conflict, retryable).

Errors:
  usage      (exit 2)  wrong number of arguments, or a name longer than 50 characters
  not_found  (exit 3)  no model of the live release has the schedule's tag and the schedule has no cron (see "schedule list")
  conflict   (exit 4)  a run is already active for this schedule, or the request id was used before with other arguments
  unavailable(exit 5)  the state service is unreachable
  maintenance(exit 7)  continuo is in maintenance mode; new work is refused until it is turned off (not retryable)
  internal   (exit 6)  unexpected server error
